title: Durian Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Durian Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Durian nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, potassium and phosphorus in duryan, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Durian nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your duryan (durian) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus, boron, calcium and magnesium. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But boron and calcium stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which durian nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a durian nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest durian nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in durian

No durian particular description was found, so this follows general fruit tree signs. The canopy turns light green, the older leaves yellow evenly and drop, and the yellowing moves up. The flush after harvest is short with small leaves, and young trees grow slowly and take longer to bear. You see it most at this stage: young trees before bearing, and bearing trees after harvest when the new flush should come.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in duryan
Native soils in many Mindanao durian areas are low in nutrients. A University of Southern Mindanao trial found even small fertilizer doses sped up growth of pre bearing trees for that reason.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium deficiency yellows old leaves between green veins. Phytophthora root and trunk rot also yellows and thins the canopy. To be sure, leaf test of the second and third leaves from the shoot tip of the first flush after harvest, taken at flowering. In a Philippine study on Chanee trees, the best yields came with leaf nitrogen of 2.22 to 2.35 percent at flowering.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

Where no soil test is done, the DA guide gives fertilizer with an NPK ratio of 12 4 7 at 100 grams per tree for the first five years, raised step by step to 4 kg per tree by the twelfth year. A Southern Mindanao trial on pre bearing trees found 400 grams Urea and 445 grams superphosphate per tree, with a small dose of Muriate of potash, enough to speed growth. Haifa puts the yearly need of bearing trees over six years old at about 1.0 to 1.8 kg nitrogen per tree, split through the season.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, fertilize right after harvest to push a strong flush, keep the ring weeded, and mulch in the dry season.
Potassium deficiency in durian

No durian particular leaf description was found, so this follows general fruit tree signs. Edges and tips of older leaves yellow and then dry brown, and the scorch moves inward. Fruit set and fruit quality fall. In a BPI Davao trial, trees that got only soil fertilizer dropped about twice as many young fruits as trees also sprayed with a high potash foliar feed. You see it most at this stage: fruit growth up to harvest, when the fruit takes the most potash.
Why potassium deficiency happens in duryan
Potash is the biggest nutrient need of bearing durian, so heavy crops drain it. Sandy and leached soils, heavy rain and long dry spells make it worse.
How to tell it apart

Fertilizer burn from a heavy dose near the trunk, and drought, also brown leaf edges. Magnesium deficiency yellows between the veins instead of along the edge. To be sure, leaf test of the second and third leaves from the shoot tip of the first flush after harvest. A soil test for exchangeable potassium.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

In a BPI Davao trial, trees given 5 kg Complete 14 14 14 per tree before flowering plus a 20 5 30 foliar feed from flower emergence to fruit growth bore 158 fruits per tree against 41 with soil fertilizer alone. A 4 0 48 foliar feed gave the sweetest flesh. A Thai orchard program used 1 kg Sulfate of potash 0 0 50 per tree during fruit growth and another 1 kg before ripening. Haifa puts the yearly need of bearing trees at about 2.1 to 4.0 kg potash per tree. Follow the soil test.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, split potash between flowering, fruit growth and before ripening, and return husks and leaves to the ring.
Phosphorus deficiency in durian

No durian particular description was found, so this follows general fruit tree signs. The tree grows slowly and older leaves turn dull with a purple or bronze tint, mostly on the underside. Flowering is weak and fewer flowers set fruit. You see it most at this stage: young trees, and bearing trees in the months before flowering.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in duryan
Acid soils that hold phosphorus tightly, and low organic matter. Leaf tests found phosphorus below the standard range in a Thai orchard.
How to tell it apart

Drought and root damage also slow growth and tint leaves. Nitrogen deficiency makes old leaves pale yellow, not purple. To be sure, leaf test of mature leaves from the last flush. Thai standards put leaf phosphorus at 0.15 to 0.25 percent.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

The Southern Mindanao trial on pre bearing trees used 445 grams superphosphate per tree with urea and potash. The Thai program gave 1 kg of a 9 25 25 fertilizer per tree before flowering. Haifa adds a leaf spray of monopotassium or ammonium phosphate at 0.5 percent (5 grams per liter) two months before flowering, three to five times two weeks apart. Lime very acid soils.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, put phosphorus in the planting hole and give a high phosphorus dose before each flowering.
Boron deficiency in durian

Flowering and fruit set are poor because pollination fails. Fruits come out small, misshapen or lopsided, the husk can crack or split, and the flesh can be corky and dry. Some fruits ripen unevenly, with hard, leathery, whitish flesh that lacks smell and taste, which shows only when opened. Leaves yellow along the edges, then brown, and can be brittle or deformed. You see it most at this stage: flowering, fruit set and fruit growth.
Why boron deficiency happens in duryan
Every crop removes boron from the tree. Sandy or leached soils low in organic matter and dry spells make it worse.
How to tell it apart

Phytophthora fruit rot gives brown, wet patches on the husk that spread, not dry cracks. Uneven ripening can also follow a new leaf flush or heavy rain during fruit growth. To be sure, leaf test and soil test for boron. The U.S.
What to apply for boron deficiency

U.S. Borax advises a leaf spray of Solubor mixed with calcium at 0.5 to 1 gram per liter from flowering through fruiting. A boron fertilizer to the soil based on tests. In a Bukidnon farm trial, foliar boron with calcium and fermented goat urine gave the most fruits per tree. Boron raised the edible portion and sweetness. Too much boron is toxic, so do not repeat high doses without a test.

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add a small boron dose each season on sandy or low boron soils, keep organic matter up, and water during dry spells.
Calcium deficiency in durian

No durian particular description was found, so this follows general fruit tree signs and keeps claims modest. Calcium does not move from old leaves to new ones. So the newest leaves, shoot tips and root tips suffer first: tips and edges of young leaves brown, and growing tips can die. Fruit quality falls. Leaf tests in a Thai orchard showed calcium well below the standard range. You see it most at this stage: new flushes and fruit growth.
Why calcium deficiency happens in duryan
Very acid, leached soils, heavy potash or ammonium fertilizer that crowds out calcium. Dry spells that slow calcium flow to the fruit.
How to tell it apart

Boron deficiency also hurts young tissue and fruit, and the two often come together, which is why sprays mix them. Leaf tip burn can also come from fertilizer or salt burn. To be sure, leaf test of mature leaves from the last flush. Thai standards put leaf calcium at 1.7 to 2.5 percent.
What to apply for calcium deficiency

On acid soils apply Agricultural lime or Dolomite in the ring, following the soil test. Where pH is fine, Gypsum adds calcium without raising pH. During flowering and fruit growth, U.S. Borax advises Solubor mixed with a calcium spray. In the Bukidnon trial foliar calcium with boron gave the best yield and return. Follow the label for calcium spray rates.

Sold here with calcium: **Planters Products Lifelime** by Planters Products, Inc. (50.59 percent CaO), **Macrock Limestone** by Donumdei 1 Corp. (36 to 42 percent calcium), **Calcic Lime** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (35.52 percent calcium) and **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer for tomatoes](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes), and the page on [calcium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/calcium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, test and lime acid soils before planting and every few years, keep potash and calcium in balance, and water during dry spells.
Magnesium deficiency in durian

No durian particular description was found, so this follows general fruit tree signs. Older leaves yellow between the veins while the veins stay dark green. In bad cases growth slows, new leaves are smaller and lower leaves drop. You see it most at this stage: bearing trees, often after heavy potash feeding and in the months before flowering.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in duryan
A leaf survey of 90 Vietnamese durian orchards found magnesium and sulfur the most deficient nutrients two months before flowering. Heavy potash, acid leached soils and heavy rain bring it on.
How to tell it apart

Potassium deficiency browns the leaf edges instead of yellowing between the veins. Nitrogen deficiency yellows the whole old leaf, veins included. To be sure, leaf test of mature leaves from the last flush, and a soil test for magnesium, potassium and calcium together.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

On acid soils apply Dolomite. Where pH is fine, use Magnesium sulfate or Kieserite, following the soil test. Haifa advises a magnesium leaf spray at 0.4 to 0.5 percent (4 to 5 grams per liter) two months after harvest, two or three times two weeks apart, to support the new flush.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use Dolomite when liming and keep potash and magnesium in balance.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any durian nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your duryan needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Durian nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my duryan leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: pale canopy, older leaves yellow and fall, and the flush after harvest comes out short and thin. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at potassium deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in durian?
items.a: Where no soil test is done, the DA guide gives fertilizer with an NPK ratio of 12 4 7 at 100 grams per tree for the first five years, raised step by step to 4 kg per tree by the twelfth year. A Southern Mindanao trial on pre bearing trees found 400 grams Urea and 445 grams superphosphate per tree, with a small dose of Muriate of potash, enough to speed growth.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in durian?
items.a: In a BPI Davao trial, trees given 5 kg Complete 14 14 14 per tree before flowering plus a 20 5 30 foliar feed from flower emergence to fruit growth bore 158 fruits per tree against 41 with soil fertilizer alone. A 4 0 48 foliar feed gave the sweetest flesh.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in durian?
items.a: The Southern Mindanao trial on pre bearing trees used 445 grams superphosphate per tree with urea and potash. The Thai program gave 1 kg of a 9 25 25 fertilizer per tree before flowering.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my duryan lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the durian nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
